title: Add request-stable strict command replay protocol
summary: Bind every strict mutation to a validated client command identity and durable route/payload fingerprint so concurrent delivery, lost-response retry, and restart replay cannot dispatch the same intent twice.
reason: Remediate the coupled P1 findings AUDIT-FIND-W01-001 and AUDIT-FIND-W07-002. A backend-only requirement would break every strict UI command, while a frontend-only identity would not prevent duplicate dispatch.
behavior_before: Every strict delivery receives a fresh server UUID and dispatches independently; the shared WebView client supplies no stable identity and encourages ordinary retry after ambiguous outcomes.
behavior_after: A new strict intent receives one validated client identity, the backend atomically reserves its canonical route/payload fingerprint before mutation, matching active deliveries report in-progress, matching completed deliveries replay durable terminal evidence, conflicting identity reuse rejects before mutation, and ambiguous client outcomes retain the exact identity for reconciliation/replay. Identity retention is bounded by the configured command-history count rather than wall-clock expiry.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_command_replay_adversarial.py: required/invalid identity rejection, atomic concurrent reservation, route/payload conflict, active duplicate block, successful response replay, lost-response replay, restart replay, malformed-journal fail-closed behavior, CORS allowance, persistence failure rollback, bounded retention, and controlled-clock coverage.

tests/webview/test_webview_api_client_command_replay_smoke.py: secure identity generation, simultaneous intent coalescing, identity retention after transport/timeout/invalid-JSON/indeterminate outcomes, no blind retry guidance, payload immutability, and fresh identity after definitive rejection.
apps/desktop/tauri/src-tauri/src/lib_tests/mod.rs: native strict request helper transmits a validated identity and rejects invalid values.

notes: Finding disposition: AUDIT-FIND-W01-001 and AUDIT-FIND-W07-002 are remediated and independently validated against current source, pre-fix red tests, immutable audit evidence, focused unit/HTTP/WebView/native-shell coverage, full-suite classification, generated checks, and strict packet coverage. Invariant: every strict mutation uses one validated request-stable identity and canonical route/payload fingerprint; the accepted reservation is durable before mutation, conflict and unresolved authority fail before mutation, and terminal replay never re-dispatches. W01-002 generic exception/indeterminate classification remains a separate batch. No external integration or representative real-media validation was required because the batch changes command delivery/evidence semantics and uses synthetic mutation fixtures.
